text:
Zoe: quick sync  spotted a discrepancy in this week's KPI deck: paid CPL dropped 18% but organic MQLs also dropped. could be attribution churn after the new tracking links. snapshot: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/weekly/kpi-03-22 :eyes:

Ethan: i dug into the dashboard filters  looks like we have two competing rules: 'utm_source precedence' and 'last_touch_cookie' fallback. they were changed in different deploys last week.

Nina: FYI the Webinar launch post was pushed Wed 21st with a shortlink variant. i also tweaked the registration form which changed one hidden field name from 'ref' -> 'source_ref'.

Marco: that's likely it. our ingestion job maps hidden fields to utm_source at parse-time. if field name changed, rows end up with null utm and fall back to cookie-based last touch, which for mobile often points to paid ad domain.

KPI-Bot: alert: channel_attrib_shift anomaly (z=3.8) detected for webinar_registrations on 2026-03-22 14:04 UTC.

Liam: running a quick comparison: raw_signups vs attributed_channel for 2026-03-21..22
```
SELECT day, attributed_channel, count(*) as n
FROM analytics.signups
WHERE campaign='rw-launch-webinar' AND day BETWEEN '2026-03-21' AND '2026-03-22'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY day, n DESC;
```

Ethan: preliminary numbers: ~1.2k regs moved from organic -> paid when utm_source is null. that explains the 18% CPL drop (artificial).

Zoe: action items: 1) @Nina revert hidden field change and redeploy form; 2) @Marco augment ingestion to check alternative field names and set a 'manual_source' flag so we can reassign in the dashboard; 3) @Liam produce an interim KPI snapshot that reassigns flagged rows back to organic for Friday deck. can we get this by EOD?

Nina: rolling back the form change now. deploying in 2m. will also add a quick test case to prevent future renames.

Marco: adding parser rule for 'source_ref' and 'ref' aliasing. also adding tracking_source tag (values: shortlink-v2, form-legacy) so we can filter in dashboard. ETA 3 hours.

Liam: i'll create a corrected KPI slice using the tracking_source tag once Marco finishes and post the before/after numbers.

KPI-Bot: note added to weekly_kpi_review (2026-03-26): shortlink/form renaming caused attribution skew. link: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/notes/3123456789-attr-note

Zoe: thanks. please include a short blurb for the deck: root cause, impact on paid CPL and organic MQLs, mitigation steps, and recommendation to re-run closed-loop MQL match after fixes.

Ethan: suggestion: for production dashboards, we should show a 'confidence' column when attribution falls back to cookie-only. small UX change but prevents headline misinterpretation.

Marco: agreed. i'll add a flag and we can surface it as an orange pill in the dashboard.

Nina: done reverting form. monitoring new signups now.

Liam: posted interim snapshot: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/perf/webinar-attr-corrected (shows paid CPL corrected, organic MQLs up ~7%).

Zoe: excellent. will mark this as an attribution note in Friday's report and recommend the confidence indicator for dashboards. closing unless anything else emerges. :lock:

KPI-Bot: auto-summary: root cause - form hidden field rename + shortlink fallback; impact - paid CPL artificially low, organic MQLs undercounted; remediation - revert form, parser aliasing, tracking_source tags; follow-up - add attribution confidence UI. archived to /shared/marketing/kpi-incidents/3123456789.json

Ethan: noted, adding to roadmap tickets. end.
